title: Who the lobbying is aimed at
question: Which officials do lobbyists contact most, for which firms and clients?
finding: Lobbyists reported 66,677 contacts with 2,873 named officials and staff from 2010 to October 2026. 33.7% were with the Planning Department and its commission, 21.6% with the Board of Supervisors and 10.9% with the Retirement System, where investment managers pitch for pension money. 11,967 contacts were with an elected official or a candidate for City office; the most contacted are Aaron Peskin (1,235), David Chiu (748), Mark Farrell (718), London N. Breed (673).
how: Each contact is one row of a lobbyist’s monthly report: official, department, date, client, subject and outcome sought. Officials are grouped by surname and first name. A person counts as elected or a candidate when the name matches someone with a campaign committee for City office and the contact is recorded at the Board, the Mayor’s office or another elected office.
limits: Lobbying is registered, and so is giving by a lobbyist’s clients and colleagues. A contact can be a meeting, a call or an e-mail, and one meeting with five officials is five rows. Senior planners and pension staff head the list because every permit and every investment pitch runs through them. Officials are named as the lobbyists typed them; two people with one name would be merged, and one person typed two ways split. Someone who once ran for office and was later contacted as appointed staff of the Mayor is counted as a candidate.
